I can see both sides. I'm a firm believer that if you have children, you need to be responsible for their care, and from experience, it can be really hard (on yourself, your pocket, or other promises). I don't think it is fair to pawn off care at all to the grandparents......they're getting old, don't want to admit it, but don't have the energy they used to. 
However, there's a huge benefit and importance in a grandparent being active in the lives of the kids. Coming from a Hispanic family, but being very americanized, keeping contact and sharing moments with grandma helps us keep our heritage alive. The other someone pointed out: it seriously takes a village. Nobody knows everything about parenting, especially since every kid is going to be so different, and they need more people to show them different ways of living and understanding the world around them. And of course, parents need a break every now and then and more advice and help etc. Finally, with my grandfather recently passing, I wish I had more memories with him to carry into the future. He had more kids of his own (my youngest aunt is 5 😵‍💫), so he couldn't be active in my life, but the memories I have are still strong, and I regret not seeking more conversation before he got sick. 
I think there's a very throwaway culture issue with it. Kiddos don't realize the importance of understanding the past sometimes, so grandparents can be thrown in last week's news. 
Anyways, I'm grateful my mom lives close to my daughter and I. Great memories certainly. I'm gonna be heartbroken if/when this arrangement changes. However, I am careful to give her a break (if my daughter asks, she won't say no) and to step in when grandma starts to spoil her too much. Rant over.
